Context
-------
Read .github/copilot-instructions.md first.

Extend the Fluent Bit deployment to collect syslog from a simulated
appliance, alongside the container-log tailing it already does.

The point of this addition is architectural, not incidental. Fluent Bit
becomes the single ingest point for three source classes:
  containers  -> tail /var/log/containers/*.log
  hosts       -> noted but not implemented (see below)
  appliances  -> syslog RFC5424 over TCP

Three benefits are being demonstrated, and the code should make them
obvious:
  1. Single configuration surface — one ConfigMap for all sources
  2. Single downstream — everything lands in the same Loki, queryable
     the same way
  3. Single airgap artifact — one image, one chart, one version

DO NOT split Fluent Bit into a second Deployment for network-received
syslog. One DaemonSet with two inputs is the point. If you find
yourself wanting to add a second Fluent Bit workload, stop and record
the reason in docs/syslog-notes.md instead.

This prompt edits files owned by earlier prompts:
  values/fluent-bit.yaml          (from prompt 3)
  templates/fluent-bit-configmap  (from prompt 3, if templated)
  app/                            (from prompt 1)
  manifests/                      (new)
  slides/slides.md                (the Slidev deck)
Make those edits carefully and add a comment at the top of each edited
file naming the prompt it originated from.

Part 1 — Sensor simulator
-------------------------
Add a new binary at app/cmd/sensor-sim. It emits RFC5424 syslog messages
to a configurable target over TCP, every ~2 seconds, forever.

Specification:
- Target from SYSLOG_TARGET env var, e.g.
    fluent-bit-syslog.observability.svc.cluster.local:5140
- Each message is a single line, well-formed RFC5424:
    <PRI>1 TIMESTAMP HOSTNAME APP-NAME PROCID MSGID STRUCTURED-DATA MSG
- PRI values: use <134> (local0.info) for routine contacts,
  <132> (local0.warning) for elevated, <131> (local0.err) for
  immediate.
- Structured data uses the example PEN 32473:
    [demo@32473 contact="submarine" bearing="045" range_nm="12" confidence="high"]
  Field values should vary plausibly — bearings 000-359, ranges 5-40nm,
  confidence high|medium|low.
- Rotate across three simulated sensors, one contact per emission:
    sonar-buoy-1, sonar-buoy-2, radar-array-1
- Message text should be short and plausible, e.g.
    "Subsurface contact classified"
    "Surface track acquired"
    "Contact lost"
- Connect once, send forever. On write failure, log and reconnect
  with a short backoff. Never exit.
- No dependencies beyond the standard library. This is a demo, not a
  product.

Build it into the same image as the other app binaries. Add a
`make sensor-sim` target alongside the existing build targets.

Part 2 — Sensor simulator manifest
----------------------------------
Create manifests/app/sensor-sim.yaml:
- Deployment, namespace demo, replicas 1
- labels: app=sensor-sim, role=syslog-source
- image pinned by tag and digest, recorded in versions.lock
- env SYSLOG_TARGET pointing at the Fluent Bit Service (see Part 3)
- resource requests: 20m CPU, 32Mi memory
- No probes needed — if it exits, restartPolicy: Always brings it back.

Part 3 — Fluent Bit ConfigMap changes
-------------------------------------
Edit the Fluent Bit ConfigMap. The existing [INPUT] for the container
tail and its [FILTER] kubernetes chain stay exactly as they are.

Add, after the existing INPUT:

  [INPUT]
      Name        syslog
      Listen      0.0.0.0
      Port        5140
      Mode        tcp
      Parser      syslog-rfc5424
      Tag         syslog.appliance

Add, after the existing FILTER chain:

  [FILTER]
      Name    record_modifier
      Match   syslog.appliance
      Record  job fluent-bit
      Record  source syslog
      Record  ingest_node ${HOSTNAME}

Add, after the existing loki OUTPUT:

  [OUTPUT]
      Name        loki
      Match       syslog.appliance
      Host        loki-gateway.observability.svc.cluster.local
      Port        80
      Labels      job=fluent-bit,source=syslog
      Label_keys  $hostname,$app_name

Add a comment block above the syslog section explaining, in the config
itself, why it is in the same file as the container tail:

  # A container log, a host log, and an appliance's syslog are the
  # same signal from three sources. One agent, one configuration,
  # one place to enforce redaction, filtering and retention.

Cardinality note: keep Loki labels minimal. Do NOT add
`sensor_id`, `contact`, `bearing` or similar as labels — those are
high-cardinality and belong in the log line, not the index. The
Label_keys above use hostname and app_name, which have small,
bounded value sets and are safe.

Part 4 — Service
----------------
Add a Service for the syslog listener in the observability namespace:
- Name: fluent-bit-syslog
- Selects the existing Fluent Bit DaemonSet pods
- Port 5140, targetPort 5140, protocol TCP
- ClusterIP is sufficient — the simulator is in-cluster
- Add a comment: if a real appliance outside the cluster is used, this
  Service needs a NodePort or a LoadBalancer, and that is a network
  policy decision, not a Fluent Bit one.

Part 5 — Verification script
----------------------------
Add scripts/syslog-send-test.sh:
- Sends a single hand-crafted RFC5424 line to the Fluent Bit Service
  over TCP, using nc or a small Go helper
- Waits 5 seconds
- Queries Loki for the marker it just sent
- Exits 0 and prints "✓ syslog path working" if found, non-zero
  otherwise

Add it to preflight.sh as a final assertion.

Part 6 — Documentation
----------------------
Create docs/syslog-notes.md covering:
- The three source classes and why the third is the hard one
- Why one agent beats three, specifically in an assurance context:
  one chokepoint to demonstrate, one config to review, one lifecycle
- The specific caveat about UDP: it is not connection-sticky across a
  Kubernetes Service, so ordering per source is not preserved. TCP is.
  If a real appliance only speaks UDP, that is a design constraint to
  name, not a problem to hide.
- The cardinality rule: fields in the log line, not in the index.
- What you would add next for a real deployment: host logs via the
  systemd input, and a note that this is deliberately omitted from the
  demo because it needs hostPath mounts on the DaemonSet.

Part 7 — Slide deck changes
---------------------------
Edit slides/slides.md (produced by the Slidev prompt). Four changes.

# 7a. Slide 3 — The signals
Below the existing four-row table, add a single muted line:
  "Container logs, host logs and appliance syslog are the same signal
   from three sources. They should land in the same place."

# 7b. Slide 5 — Why this stack
Add one row to the table:
  Ingest | One agent for containers, hosts and appliances

Keep the Criterion column in accent mono, consistent with the rest.

# 7c. New backup slide
Add a new backup slide after the existing last one. This makes the deck
18 slides, not 17. Update any slide count assertion accordingly.

  Title: One agent, three sources
  A three-line flow, each line an input path with its tag:

    containers   tail /var/log/containers/*.log      tag: kube.*
    hosts        systemd / journald (not in demo)    tag: host.*
    appliances   syslog RFC5424, TCP 5140            tag: syslog.appliance

  Below the flow, a single line:
    "Same ConfigMap. Same Loki. Same query surface."

  Below that, in muted smaller text:
    "One place to enforce redaction, filtering and retention."

# 7d. Slide 2 note
Update the speaker note for slide 2 to add one sentence at the end:
  "And the sources are not just containers. A twenty-year-old sensor
   array that only speaks syslog belongs in the same place as a modern
   service — and can be, with the same agent."

Part 8 — Update the speaker notes
---------------------------------
Regenerate slides/speaker-notes.md using the same generation rules as
prompt 8 (read the actual repo state, do not invent names). The new
backup slide and the slide 2 addition both need notes.

Also regenerate docs/demo-runbook.md so beat 7 (Logs) reflects the new
flourish described in Part 9.

Part 9 — Beat 7 (Logs) flavour change
-------------------------------------
The runbook's beat 7 currently ends with an optional flourish that
flips the Fluent Bit output to a file and back. REPLACE that flourish
with the syslog demonstration below. The new flourish is longer
(~60s vs ~20s) but replaces a weaker version of the same argument.

Insert this as the final action in beat 7, after the container-log
query:

  Query Loki for the syslog path:
    {source="syslog"} |= "contact"

  Narration, in the presenter's voice:
    "Same pipeline. This is coming in over TCP syslog from a sensor
     appliance — the kind of kit that only speaks syslog and has been
     doing so since before Kubernetes existed. It lands in the same
     Loki, sits next to the container logs, and is queryable the same
     way. One agent, one configuration file, one place to enforce what
     gets redacted and what gets retained. If you have three
     collectors, you have three policies to prove."

  Then show the syslog path in the same view:
    {source="syslog"} | json | pri <= 132
  "Warnings and above. Same syntax as the container logs."

Update the beat 7 duration from 4 to 5 minutes. The total content
becomes 36 minutes, leaving 4 minutes of slack in the 40-minute slot.
Cut order is unchanged: 7, then 6, then 8, with 4 (Torpedo) and
5 (DNS) never cut.

Constraints
-----------
- One Fluent Bit DaemonSet. Do not add a second Fluent Bit workload.
- Do not add high-cardinality Loki labels.
- Do not modify any part of the existing container-log path.
- Every image pinned by tag and digest, recorded in versions.lock.
- Everything must work with the network interface down, except the
  initial build. A syslog sender inside the cluster is in-boundary
  traffic and needs no special treatment.
- The simulator must never exit on its own. If it does, that is a bug.

Acceptance
----------
1. `./scripts/syslog-send-test.sh` exits 0 with "✓ syslog path working".
2. A hand-sent RFC5424 line appears in Loki within 10 seconds when
   queried with `{source="syslog"}`.
3. The sensor-sim Deployment has been running for 60 seconds with
   restartCount 0.
4. The container-log path still works unchanged:
   `{namespace="demo"}` returns application logs as before.
5. `preflight.sh` passes clean, including the new syslog assertion.
6. `slides/export.pdf` now has 18 pages, not 17.
7. The BeatCounter in slides/components/BeatCounter.vue is unchanged —
   still 10 beats. Syslog is a flavour in beat 7, not a new beat.
Report the results of checks 1, 2 and 6.
